name: Currency switch from the header and price conversion
step_description: Open http://localhost:8080/ in a fresh private window (kubectl port-forward deployment/frontend 8080:8080) and open the currency dropdown in the header.
description: Checks setCurrencyHandler and the whitelist of six currencies on the home page, with the ECB figures from data/currency_conversion.json. Needs the Online Boutique stack with the frontend port-forwarded to localhost:8080 and the browser network tab.

step_description: The dropdown lists EUR, USD, JPY, GBP, TRY and CAD with USD selected; Sunglasses shows $19.99 and Mug $8.99.
Select EUR in the dropdown and inspect the POST /setCurrency response in the network tab.
HTTP 302 back to the home page with Set-Cookie shop_currency=EUR; Max-Age=172800; the page now shows Sunglasses €17.68 and Mug €7.95.
curl -i -d currency_code=ABC http://localhost:8080/setCurrency
HTTP 422 and the body contains "Field 'Currency' is invalid: iso4217"; reloading the browser tab still shows the EUR prices.

name: Add to cart with quantities, accumulation and the 1 to 10 limit
step_description: On http://localhost:8080/product/OLJCESPC7Z choose quantity 2 and click Add To Cart.
description: Checks addToCartHandler validation and the cartservice quantity accumulation through the UI and one direct POST. The shop_session-id cookie is copied from the browser for the curl step.

step_description: The browser lands on /cart showing Cart (2), one Sunglasses line at $39.98, Shipping $8.99 and Total $48.97.
Go back to the Sunglasses page, choose quantity 3 and add it again.
/cart still has a single Sunglasses line, now with quantity 5, and the header badge shows 5.
curl -i -b "shop_session-id=<value from the browser>" -d "product_id=OLJCESPC7Z&quantity=11" http://localhost:8080/cart
HTTP 422 with "Field 'Quantity' is invalid: lte" and /cart still shows quantity 5.

name: Declined card shows a checkout message instead of an error page
step_description: With one Mug in the cart, fill the checkout form with card number 378282246310005 (AMEX test number), any future expiry and CVV 672, and click Place Order.
description: Acceptance of the fix for the HTTP 500 on CreditCardError: an unaccepted card type and an expired card must come back as HTTP 400 with the paymentservice message. Left in phase New until the fix is deployed.

step_description: The response is HTTP 400 and the page shows "Sorry, we cannot process amex credit cards. Only VISA or MasterCard is accepted." with no rpc error chain; /cart still holds the Mug.

curl -i -b "shop_session-id=<value>" -d "email=someone@example.com&street_address=1600+Amphitheatre+Parkway&zip_code=94043&city=Mountain+View&state=CA&country=United+States&credit_card_number=4432801561520454&credit_card_expiration_month=1&credit_card_expiration_year=2020&credit_card_cvv=672" http://localhost:8080/cart/checkout
HTTP 400 with "Your credit card (ending 0454) expired on 1/2020"; the paymentservice log shows the same message and no "Transaction processed" line.

name: Flat shipping quote and tracking id format
step_description: With an empty cart and the currency on USD, add one Mug and open /cart.
description: Regression check of the shipped quote logic covered by TestGetQuote and TestTrackingIdFormat in the local CI: USD 8.99 whatever the quantity, and an 18-character tracking id with the default address.

step_description: Shipping $8.99 and Total $17.98.
Add the Watch with quantity 10 and reload /cart.
Shipping is still $8.99; the lines read $8.99 and $1099.90 and the Total is $1117.88.
Place the order with the default form values.
The Tracking # is 18 characters and matches ^[A-Z]{2}-44\d{3}-22\d{7}$ for the default address (the digit groups start with the salt length 44 and its half 22).

name: Product catalog lookups and catalog reloading
step_description: kubectl port-forward deployment/productcatalogservice 3550:3550, then grpcurl -plaintext -import-path protos -proto demo.proto -d '{"id":"OLJCESPC7Z"}' localhost:3550 hipstershop.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct
description: Regression of the catalog RPCs covered by the four go tests in the local CI, plus the SIGUSR1 reload switch from the service README. Uses grpcurl with protos/demo.proto against a port-forward on 3550.

step_description: name Sunglasses, priceUsd units 19 and nanos 990000000, categories [accessories].
Repeat GetProduct with id abc005, then call SearchProducts with query MUG.
GetProduct answers code NotFound with "no product with ID abc005"; SearchProducts returns exactly one result, id 6E92ZMYYFZ.
kubectl exec deployment/productcatalogservice -- kill -USR1 1, load the home page twice, then kill -USR2 1 and load it twice more.
The log shows "Enable catalog reloading" followed by one "loading catalog from local products.json file..." per request, then "Disable catalog reloading" with no further loading lines.

name: Checkout in EUR: totals, logs and emptied cart
step_description: Set the currency to EUR, add Sunglasses with quantity 2 and open /cart.
description: Walks the PlaceOrder flow end to end with the currency set to EUR and checks the figures from the ECB table, the order page, the checkoutservice and emailservice logs and the emptied cart.

step_description: The line reads €35.36, Shipping €7.95 and Total €43.31.
Submit the checkout form with its default values (someone@example.com, 1600 Amphitheatre Parkway, 94043, Mountain View, CA, United States, card 4432801561520454, CVV 672).
The order page shows a Confirmation # in UUID form, a Tracking # matching ^[A-Z]{2}-\d+-\d+$ and Total Paid €43.31.

kubectl logs deployment/checkoutservice contains [PlaceOrder] with user_currency="EUR", "payment went through (transaction_id:" and "order confirmation email sent to "someone@example.com""; kubectl logs deployment/emailservice contains "A request to send order confirmation email to someone@example.com has been received."
GET /cart shows "Your shopping cart is empty!" and the header has no badge.

name: Ads follow the product category
step_description: Open http://localhost:8080/product/OLJCESPC7Z (Sunglasses, category accessories) five times.
description: Checks AdService.getAds through the frontend: a category with one ad always shows it, a category with two alternates between them, and the ad block links to the advertised product.

step_description: Each time the Ad block reads "Watch for sale. Buy one, get second kit for free" and links to /product/1YMWWN1N4O in a new tab.
Open http://localhost:8080/product/6E92ZMYYFZ (Mug, category kitchen) ten times.
The ad is either "Bamboo glass jar for sale. 10% off." (/product/9SIQT8TOJO) or "Mug for sale. Buy two, get third one for free" (/product/6E92ZMYYFZ), and both appear at least once.

name: Batch numbering and PreserveBatchNumbers on POST /files/create
step_description: docker run -p 8080:8080 moov/ach:v1.68.0, then curl -s -i -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @server/test/unordered_batches/Moov-batch-numbers-issue.json http://localhost:8080/files/create
description: Checks File.Create renumbering and the preserveBatchNumbers and unorderedBatchNumbers query options on the moov/ach HTTP server with the unordered-batches sample from the repository (two CCD batches numbered 2 then 1).

step_description: HTTP 200 with a JSON id and "error": null; GET /files/<id>/contents shows the two batch header records numbered 0000001 then 0000002 (Create renumbered 2, 1 in write order).
Repeat the POST with ?preserveBatchNumbers=true.
HTTP 500 and the body contains "Batch numbers must be in ascending order, batch 1 is less than or equal to the previous batch: 2".
Repeat the POST with ?preserveBatchNumbers=true&unorderedBatchNumbers=true and fetch GET /files/<id>/contents.
HTTP 200 with an id, and the contents keep the batch numbers 0000002 then 0000001.

name: Latin-1 bytes in a written Nacha file via achcli
step_description: go build ./cmd/achcli in the ach clone, then ./achcli -reformat=json test/testdata/ppd-debit.ach > /tmp/ppd.json and change the entry's individualName to "José Receiver".
description: Regression of the ISO-8859-1 writer (commit 3f6ca97) using achcli built from the clone: a name with é must stay on a 94-byte line as byte E9 and read back as UTF-8.

step_description: ./achcli -reformat=ach /tmp/ppd.json > /tmp/ppd-latin1.ach
LC_ALL=C awk '{ print length($0) }' /tmp/ppd-latin1.ach prints 94 for every line, and xxd /tmp/ppd-latin1.ach shows the byte e9 in the entry detail line with no c3 a9 sequence.
./achcli /tmp/ppd-latin1.ach describes the entry with Name "José Receiver" (read back as UTF-8).
